learningObjective: Compare the arithmetic density (FLOP per cycle per SM) of NVIDIA Tensor Core FP16 vs FP32 SIMT paths, and reason about when each dominates.

canonicalClaims.claim: On A100 SXM, dense FP16 Tensor Core peak throughput is approximately 16× the FP32 CUDA-core peak (312 TFLOP/s vs 19.5 TFLOP/s), so compute-bound kernels that can adopt FP16 Tensor Cores may approach a 16× ideal speedup; memory-bound kernels see much smaller gains.
conditions: Kernel is compute-bound (AI > ridge point for the target path).
Precision can safely be reduced to FP16 with matching accumulation strategy.
Kernel uses Tensor Cores, not the FP16 scalar path in CUDA cores.
nonImplications: Does not imply any kernel automatically reaches 16× speedup.
Does not imply comparable ratios apply to all architectures; H100 and later revise the numbers.

misconceptions.claim: FP16 Tensor Core is roughly 2× FP32 CUDA-core throughput.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The ratio is ~16× on A100, not 2×. 2× is closer to the SIMT FP16 vs FP32 pathway.

misconceptions.claim: Sparse Tensor Core peak is what appears in the 312 TFLOP/s figure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The 312 TFLOP/s A100 SXM figure is dense. Sparse (2:4) FP16 gives 624 TFLOP/s.

misconceptions.claim: Using FP16 Tensor Cores yields ~16× end-to-end speedup on any DNN workload.
misconceptions.whyWrong: End-to-end speedup depends on the mix of memory-bound vs compute-bound ops; memory-bound ops are limited by HBM bandwidth, which is unchanged.

implementationFacts: A100 SXM dense: FP32 CUDA ≈ 19.5 TFLOP/s; FP16 Tensor Core ≈ 312 TFLOP/s; BF16 similar to FP16.
H100 SXM5 FP16 Tensor Core dense ≈ 989 TFLOP/s; FP8 dense ≈ 1979 TFLOP/s.
performanceScenarios: Mixed-precision training on A100 achieves 3–6× kernel speedup on GEMM-dominant workloads and less on memory-bound layers.
